value.body:
Jack Heart, 2026-11-13: "https://softmax.com/hanabi is of interest to me, maybe we could find another implementation of hanabi", then linked https://github.com/google-deepmind/hanabi-learning-environment.

Looked up the same day:
- Softmax Hanabi is a live Coworld: Hanabi for four LLM-piloted players, one shared score, a league with a leaderboard; a search summary of the page says a policy there "is just a prompt". The page itself did not render for a plain fetch. A Coworld (softmax.com/docs/coworld/build-a-coworld/overview) packages "the game, its player protocol, baseline players, documentation, and a fixture" behind a `coworld_manifest.json`, with a `coworld` CLI (run-episode, play, certify, upload-coworld). Framework: github.com/softmax-universe/coworld (pushed 2026-11-13, no licence recorded on the repository). Whether the Hanabi game is open source or runs locally was not established. Unread and likely to answer it: softmax.com/hanabi/hanabi/onboarding.md, softmax.com/docs/coworld/build-a-player/overview.
- DeepMind Hanabi Learning Environment: Apache-2.0, C++ with a Python wrapper, archived, last push 2023-02, last code change 2021. The reference rules implementation.
- JaxMARL (github.com/FLAIROx/JaxMARL): Apache-2.0, includes Hanabi in JAX, pushed 2026-10-26, not archived.
- Not checked: PettingZoo or OpenSpiel Hanabi wrappers, and whether PufferLib has Hanabi.

Hanabi suits this Task as the shared game: two to five seats, a shared score rather than win or loss, and value measured with unfamiliar partners, which are exactly the evaluation cases named in the Outcome.
